entries.name: François Arago
entries.background: Prominent 19th-century French astronomer, physicist, and statesman known for contributions to optics and electromagnetism.

entries.name: fragmented science
entries.senseHere: A field of study split into disconnected pockets of researchers working on separate theories, data sets, and lab experiments without a shared framework or agreement.

entries.name: Pyotr Leonidovich Kapitsa
entries.background: Soviet physicist and Nobel laureate renowned for his research in low-temperature physics and strong magnetic fields.

entries.name: Wilhelm von Haidinger
entries.background: 19th-century Austrian geologist and mineralogist who helped found Austria's geological survey and was a member of the Imperial Academy of Sciences at Vienna.

entries.name: Othniel Charles Marsh
entries.background: Prominent 19th-century American paleontologist famous for his fierce fossil-hunting rivalry with Edward Drinker Cope, known as the Bone Wars, which helped establish American dinosaur science.

entries.name: Walther Gerlach
entries.background: German physicist best known for co-discovering the quantization of electron spin in a magnetic field in 1922, a landmark experiment in the development of quantum mechanics.

entries.name: Roger Clifton Jennison
entries.background: British radio astronomer who worked at the Jodrell Bank Observatory and later became a professor of physical electronics, known for pioneering work in astronomical interferometry.

entries.name: Georg Wilhelm Richmann
entries.background: Baltic-German physicist who died in 1753 while experimenting with atmospheric electricity, becoming one of the earliest scientists killed in the study of electricity.

entries.name: keraunoparalysis
entries.senseHere: The short-lived nerve and muscle effects of a lightning or ball lightning strike, such as temporary paralysis or numbness, as opposed to lasting psychological or nerve damage.
entries.background: This is a recognized clinical term in medicine for lightning-related paralysis, still used by doctors today to describe transient post-strike symptoms.

entries.name: Jean-Martin Charcot
entries.background: Pioneering 19th-century French neurologist often called the founder of modern neurology, famous for his studies of hysteria and nervous disorders, and for teaching a young Sigmund Freud.
